construction_notes: The dependent variable is the 'social well-being' index of the Danish National Well-Being Survey, constructed following the official guide of the Ministry/Agency from 10 items; approximately continuous, ranging from 1 to 5 including decimals; Cronbach’s alpha 0.87.
Only the social well-being dimension of the four well-being dimensions is used; academic well-being, support and inspiration, and classroom noise/punctuality are deliberately not included.
The exposure is pooled across the three waves and set to the respondent’s latest observed activity status (sports active / sports inactive).
All covariates are measured at T − 1: at the end of 2020, or accumulated throughout 2020 (employment measured as total working hours in 2020).
Missing data handled by complete-case analysis; participant flow documented in Figure S1 of the Supplementary Materials.
Treatment model: logit; outcome model: linear regression; estimation in Stata 17.0.

Descriptives (Table 2, p. 8): 27.6% (276) sports inactive and 72.4% (723) sports participants of 999; 2020 mean well-being 4.10 (0.69) for the inactive, 4.28 (0.54) for participants, 4.23 (0.59) in total; 2022 mean well-being 3.95 (0.63), 4.14 (0.56) and 4.09 (0.59) respectively.
Among the sports-active group, 63% participate in a team sport and 37% in an individual sport (not shown in a table).
Of 301 sports active respondents in Wave 1, 258 remain active in Wave 2 (86%); of 397 sports active in Wave 2, 359 (90%) remained active in Wave 3.

ambiguities: The paper calls its estimand an ATE (ATĒ_AIPW in the estimating equation) but states repeatedly that no causal claim is made; identification.strategy is recorded as selection_on_observables because the design is adjustment for observed covariates, not because the paper claims causal identification.

ambiguities: The paper calls its estimand an ATE (ATĒ_AIPW in the estimating equation) but states repeatedly that no causal claim is made; identification.strategy is recorded as selection_on_observables because the design is adjustment for observed covariates, not because the paper claims causal identification.
The paper prints no clustering or inference details beyond 'Standard errors are in parentheses'.
The table legend prints '* = 0.05. ** = 0.01 *** = 0.001.'; the p-value is recorded with p_value_relation 'less_than' following the conventional reading of significance stars.
Table 4 reports no confidence intervals and the paper gives no separate n for the estimation sample of each exploratory contrast beyond the group sizes given in the text.
The n recorded (486) is the panel total printed in the Table 4 panel header; the number actually used after excluding respondents who changed status is not printed.
One of the three exposure measurements (spring 2022) is contemporaneous with the spring 2022 outcome, so the 'latest observed status' is not always strictly prior to the outcome.
